title: Proving Triangles Congruent: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and HL
seo_title: Geometry Proving Triangles Congruent Worksheets (TEKS G.6B)
standard_text: G.6B prove two triangles are congruent by applying the Side-Angle-Side, Angle-Side-Angle, Side-Side-Side, Angle-Angle-Side, and Hypotenuse-Leg congruence conditions; G.6C apply the definition of congruence, in terms of rigid transformations, to identify congruent figures and their corresponding sides and angles
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.6B and G.6C: prove triangles congruent with SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and HL, corresponding parts and CPCTC. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, HL — never AAA or SSA.
key_sub: △ABC ≅ △DEF: A ↔ D, B ↔ E, C ↔ F.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Triangles are congruent when a rigid transformation maps one onto the other.
  • Criteria: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and HL for right triangles.
  • AAA and SSA do not prove congruence.
  • The order of letters matters: △ABC ≅ △DEF means A ↔ D, B ↔ E, C ↔ F.

Examples

Example

Two sides and the included angle are congruent

the angle is between the sides

Answer: SAS

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using AAA or SSAThey are not criteria.
Matching parts in the wrong orderFollow the letter order.
Forgetting a shared sideA shared side is congruent to itself.

items.q: Given △QPZ ≅ △RNM, which segment is congruent to QZ?
items.e: Match the letters in order: Q → R and Z → M. So QZ ≅ RM.

items.q: Given △DQT ≅ △GVE, which segment is congruent to QT?
items.e: Match the letters in order: Q → V and T → E. So QT ≅ VE.

items.q: Given △YZM ≅ △NRD, which angle is congruent to ∠Y?
items.e: Y is in the same position as N in the statement, so ∠Y ≅ ∠N.

items.q: Given △LYX ≅ △AMV, which angle is congruent to ∠X?
items.e: X is in the same position as V in the statement, so ∠X ≅ ∠V.

items.q: Given △LWA ≅ △TQC, which segment is congruent to AW?

items.q: Given △AKJ ≅ △UXE, complete the statement: △JAK ≅ ?
items.e: Keep each pair of matching vertices together: J ↔ E, A ↔ U, K ↔ X. So △JAK ≅ △EUX.

items.e: Match the letters in order: A → U and G → T. So AG ≅ UT.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, ∠R and ∠Z are right angles, and PQ ≅ XY (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by HL?
items.e: HL needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. PR and XZ are legs: PR ≅ XZ.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, ∠P ≅ ∠X and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as QR: QR ≅ YZ.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, ∠R ≅ ∠U and ∠S ≅ ∠V. What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. RS is between ∠R and ∠S: RS ≅ UV.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, ∠G ≅ ∠L and ∠H ≅ ∠M. What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. GH is between ∠G and ∠H: GH ≅ LM.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠A ≅ ∠D and ∠B ≅ ∠E. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as BC: BC ≅ EF.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠A ≅ ∠D and ∠B ≅ ∠E. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. AB is between ∠A and ∠B: AB ≅ DE.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, JK ≅ MN and KL ≅ NO. What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: JL ≅ MO.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, RS ≅ UV and ∠S ≅ ∠V. What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠S is between RS and ST: ST ≅ VW.

items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: RT ≅ UW.

△GHK ≅ △LMN. m∠G = 52°, m∠H = 47° and m∠N = (5x + 31)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠N corresponds to ∠K, so m∠K = 180 − 52 − 47 = 81. Then 5x + 31 = 81, so x = 10.

items.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. m∠A = 39°, m∠C = 66° and m∠E = (4x + 19)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠E corresponds to ∠B, so m∠B = 180 − 39 − 66 = 75. Then 4x + 19 = 75, so x = 14.

items.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. CB = 5x − 2 and FE = 8. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCTC): CB = FE, so 5x − 2 = 8 and x = 2.

items.e: ∠U corresponds to ∠R, so m∠R = 180 − 59 − 69 = 52. Then 3x + 25 = 52, so x = 9.

items.q: △PQR ≅ △XYZ. RQ = 4x − 19 and ZY = 21. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCTC): RQ = ZY, so 4x − 19 = 21 and x = 10.

items.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. AB = 3x + 5 and DE = 14. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCTC): AB = DE, so 3x + 5 = 14 and x = 3.

items.q: △RPQ ≅ △ZXY. PQ = 15, QR = 18 and PR = 18. What is the perimeter of △XYZ?
items.e: Congruent triangles have congruent corresponding sides, so the perimeters are equal: 15 + 18 + 18 = 51.

items.q: △RTS ≅ △UWV. m∠R = 36° and m∠W = 79°. Find m∠V.
items.e: ∠R matches ∠U, and ∠W matches ∠T. The third angle is 180 − 36 − 79 = 65°.

items.q: In the figure, which shortcut proves △ABD ≅ △CBD?
items.e: AB ≅ CB and AD ≅ CD are marked. BD ≅ BD by the Reflexive Property (a shared side). Three pairs of sides: SSS.

items.q: Is AAA a way to prove two triangles congruent?
c: Yes, if the angles are acute
No, because triangles have only two angles
No, because the triangles can be different sizes
items.e: Two equilateral triangles with sides 2 and 5 have the same angles but are not congruent. No, because the triangles can be different sizes.

items.q: △KGH ≅ △NLM. m∠G = 78° and m∠N = 46°. Find m∠M.
items.e: ∠G matches ∠L, and ∠N matches ∠K. The third angle is 180 − 78 − 46 = 56°.

items.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. Which must be true?
c: The triangles have the same orientation
items.e: All corresponding sides are equal, so the perimeters are equal. Orientation can change with a reflection. The perimeters are equal.

items.q: △HGK ≅ △MLN. m∠H = 55° and m∠N = 44°. Find m∠L.
items.e: ∠H matches ∠M, and ∠N matches ∠K. The third angle is 180 − 55 − 44 = 81°.

items.q: △KGH ≅ △NLM. m∠H = 31° and m∠N = 41°. Find m∠L.
items.e: ∠H matches ∠M, and ∠N matches ∠K. The third angle is 180 − 31 − 41 = 108°.

items.q: △SRT ≅ △VUW. m∠S = 46° and m∠W = 75°. Find m∠U.
items.e: ∠S matches ∠V, and ∠W matches ∠T. The third angle is 180 − 46 − 75 = 59°.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent if one can be mapped onto the other by
c: A sequence of dilations and translations
items.e: Congruence is defined by rigid motions (translations, reflections, rotations), which keep sizes the same. A sequence of rigid motions.

items.q: Is SSA a way to prove two triangles congruent?
c: Yes, it is the same as SAS
No, because two different triangles can have the same SSA parts
No, because a triangle has no SSA parts
items.e: The angle is not between the sides, so the third side can swing to two places. No, because two different triangles can have the same SSA parts.

items.q: △STR ≅ △VWU. m∠S = 69° and m∠W = 54°. Find m∠U.
items.e: ∠S matches ∠V, and ∠W matches ∠T. The third angle is 180 − 69 − 54 = 57°.

items.q: △GHK ≅ △LMN. m∠G = 45° and m∠M = 63°. Find m∠N.
items.e: ∠G matches ∠L, and ∠M matches ∠H. The third angle is 180 − 45 − 63 = 72°.

items.q: △BAC ≅ △EDF. m∠A = 75° and m∠E = 40°. Find m∠F.
items.e: ∠A matches ∠D, and ∠E matches ∠B. The third angle is 180 − 75 − 40 = 65°.

items.q: What does CPCTC stand for?
c: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent
Congruent parts can prove triangles congruent
Corresponding points create two congruent triangles
items.e: Once triangles are proved congruent, every pair of corresponding sides and angles is congruent. Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent.

items.q: Segments AC and BD bisect each other at M. Which shortcut proves △AMB ≅ △CMD?
items.e: AM ≅ CM and BM ≅ DM. ∠AMB ≅ ∠CMD because they are vertical angles, and that angle is between the two pairs of sides: SAS.

items.q: △RST ≅ △UVW. RS = 13, ST = 11 and RT = 6. What is the perimeter of △UVW?
items.e: Congruent triangles have congruent corresponding sides, so the perimeters are equal: 13 + 11 + 6 = 30.

items.q: △RST ≅ △UVW. m∠R = 83° and m∠W = 60°. Find m∠V.
items.e: ∠R matches ∠U, and ∠W matches ∠T. The third angle is 180 − 83 − 60 = 37°.

items.q: △HKG ≅ △MNL. m∠G = 76° and m∠N = 30°. Find m∠M.
items.e: ∠G matches ∠L, and ∠N matches ∠K. The third angle is 180 − 76 − 30 = 74°.

items.q: △CAB ≅ △FDE. m∠A = 85° and m∠F = 30°. Find m∠E.
items.e: ∠A matches ∠D, and ∠F matches ∠C. The third angle is 180 − 85 − 30 = 65°.
